questions.title: What do you make?
questions.hint: Choose the closest match. We’ll tailor the assessment to your operation.
options: Parts made using moulds or tooling
Designed or engineered for a customer

questions.title: How many people work in your business?
questions.hint: Include the shop floor and office. Team size alone won’t decide your recommendation.

questions.title: What gets production moving?
questions.hint: Think about how most of your work begins.
options: Engineering is part of the job

questions.title: How many active parts or products do you manage?
questions.hint: A rough estimate is fine. Include materials and components you actively manage.

questions.title: How many stages does a typical job pass through?
questions.hint: For example: cutting, machining, finishing, then assembly.

questions.title: What has to come together to finish a job?
questions.hint: Select everything you regularly coordinate.

questions.title: Where does your production information live?
questions.hint: Choose the description that feels most like your working day.
options: ERP or MRP, with significant workarounds
A connected system that largely meets our needs

questions.title: What is prompting you to consider a change?
questions.hint: Sometimes improving an existing system is the best next step.
options: Support or reliability is a problem
It’s difficult to use or poorly adopted
Our setup or data needs attention

questions.title: An urgent order arrives. What happens next?
questions.hint: How do you work out what can move?
options: We ask around and use experience
Our system shows capacity and the impact

questions.title: How do you know what to buy, and when?
questions.hint: Manual methods can work well. We’ll consider this alongside the problems you experience.

questions.title: Do you meet the delivery dates you promise?
questions.hint: Think about a typical month, rather than your best or worst week.

questions.title: What would you most like to improve?
questions.hint: Choose up to three. It’s fine if things are working well.

questions.title: Which would make the biggest difference?
questions.hint: We’ll use this to prioritise your action plan.

questions.title: How often do those problems disrupt work?
questions.hint: Consider their impact across the operation.

questions.title: How much time goes into chasing, re-keying and replanning?
questions.hint: Estimate the combined time across your team each week.

questions.title: What seems to be driving the problems?
questions.hint: Choose up to two. Your best judgement is enough.
options: Not enough people or machine capacity

questions.title: What will change in the next 12–24 months?
questions.hint: Select confirmed changes, or tell us if growth is still an ambition.
options: Growth is an ambition, not yet committed

questions.title: How dependable are your production records?
questions.hint: Think about stock quantities, part details and production information.

questions.title: Could someone lead a systems improvement project?
questions.hint: This helps us suggest a realistic next step.
options: Yes, with management support and time
Someone could, but time is tight
There isn’t a clear owner yet

questions.title: What would a new system have to do?
questions.hint: Select your essentials. These help us assess Fraction separately from your need for ERP.
options: Work offline or run on our own servers

questions.title: Which specialist requirement is essential?
questions.hint: Choose the closest match. We’ll flag anything that needs a detailed review.
options: Multiple legal entities or group consolidation
A specific machine or software integration
Offline working or an on-premise installation
